fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review with thematic analysis. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis themes (Table 3 and the sections on training data and resume screening): stereotyping in voice assistants, image recognition and language models, indirect discrimination through resume keywords linked to men, lower accuracy for inputs involving women. AN_Task Other_Task: recruitment and resume screening as the AI application the review discusses. Mitigation: representative datasets (Pre_Processing), diverse teams, ethics boards, mentorship and digital literacy programmes (Organisational_Process), all recommended; the AI4ALL figures report career interest, not bias reduction, so the status stays Proposed. Adversarial debiasing is only named as a popular technique and is not coded as In_Training. The intersectionality section uses rural versus urban women as an example of access barriers, not of AI bias, so Intersectional is not coded in AN_Bias_Axes or AN_Gender_Understanding. Gender appears throughout as women versus men without a definition.

fields.AN_Notes: Illustrative case study with artifact analysis of nine educators in an online AI in Education course. Prompts in the 'Experimenting With Algorithmic Bias' activity serve to elicit model output as a bias probe, hence Research_Instrument; no named technique. Bias axes follow the work's own findings: gender (CEO images) and cultural bias, which the work names as cultural (country depictions), coded as Language_Culture. Harm types come from the findings on participant artifacts: stereotypes, misleading representations of cultures and the male default for CEO images. Mitigation: the critical co-discovery course itself as training of educators (Organisational_Process), implemented and analysed without an assessed bias outcome, hence Demonstrated. Gender appears only as men and women in the findings. Theory reference: the framing of generative AI as a socio-technical system that perpetuates inequalities and biases frames the treatment of bias; constructivism and speculative design frame only the pedagogy.

fields.AN_Notes: Qualitative interview study with tech workers at one company, interpreted through feminist theory of responsibility. Bias axes: the work's own argument for revaluing maintenance work rests on its gendered and racialized distribution in the AI industry (section 'Seeing the bigger picture'), coded as Gender and Race_Ethnicity; this is a structural argument about labour, not a measurement of model bias. Mitigation: organisational recommendations (response-ability, revaluing care and maintenance, collective cultures of responsibility, ethics committees discussed), Proposed. fields.AN_Notes: Reflexive thematic analysis of interviews with 21 clinical social workers in private practice, framed by the Technology Acceptance Model. Prompting: interviewers entered a participant's case dilemma into ChatGPT to demonstrate model output during the interview, coded as Research_Instrument; participants' own prompting is described, not recommended, and has no named technique. Bias appears as participant concern ('Bias and Equity' subtheme); participants mention racism, ethnicity and wealth only as questions or enumerations, so no axis is coded (None) and no harm mechanism is established by the work. Bias understanding is recognisable as reproduction of systemic inequities through training data (Implicit_Only). Mitigation: professional guidelines, institutional safeguards and social work education on critical algorithmic literacy, Proposed. Tasks from the findings: documentation and notes, treatment planning and decision-making, client engagement and what to say to clients, e-mails and scheduling, supervision of supervisees. TAM frames technology acceptance, not gender or bias, so AN_Theory_Reference No.

fields.AN_Notes: Philosophical analysis of the dominant parity-based interpretation of intersectional fairness. Bias axes from the work's own worked examples: race and gender in their intersection (Black women, Asian women in the hiring example), nonbinary and trans people under cisnormativity in the scanner example (Sexual_Orientation_Identity). The AM1/AM2 example uses visa status and alma mater only to illustrate subgroup regress and is not coded as an axis. Harm types: the face recognition case is cited but its causal mechanism is analysed in the work's own argument (Disparate_Performance); the self-constructed hiring algorithm prefers white male applicants by learning the group attributes from past data, coded as Direct_Discrimination although the work does not classify it as direct or indirect; cisnormativity built into scanners (Exclusionary_Norms) and the absence of nonbinary gender as a category (Erasure). Representational harms from Noble's search examples are cited and not coded. Mitigation: shift to non-distributive strong fairness, redesign of the development process and community and cross-disciplinary collaboration (Organisational_Process), Proposed. AN_Task Other_Task: hiring, admissions, loan approval and recidivism risk prediction as AI decision tasks outside social work.

fields.AN_Notes: Framework study that re-annotates Social Chemistry and Dynahate instances with LabintheWild volunteers and correlates demographic groups with dataset labels and model predictions (Delphi, GPT-4, Perspective API, Rewire API, ToxiGen RoBERTa). Zero-shot prompt templates evaluate GPT-4, coded as Research_Instrument without a named technique. Axes compared in Table 2 and the results text: gender (man, woman, non-binary), ethnicity, age, education level (Socioeconomic), native language and cultural spheres of country (Language_Culture, the name the work gives the country grouping), religion (Table 2 only). Intersectional is not coded: the limitations state that Pearson's r does not consider interaction effects. Harm types: design bias as groups for whom datasets and models work less well (Disparate_Performance) and imposition of Western standards (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation recommendations: recruiting diverse annotators, disaggregated annotations and careful label aggregation (Pre_Processing); documenting design choices, reporting positionality, participatory and value-sensitive design, diverse teams (Organisational_Process), all Proposed. Social acceptability and hate speech detection are evaluated as NLP benchmark tasks without a professional application task, AN_Task None. Gender categories include non-binary as a category of analysis without a definition of gender.
